Subject: MSA/Order Form: liability caps & SLA credit interaction

Hi Monica,

We reviewed the MSA + Order Form you sent and have a couple of points from Legal/Procurement we need to resolve before we can proceed:

1) Limitation of liability — Celsius's general position is a monetary cap equal to 12 months of fees (prior 12 months) for direct damages, with an explicit exclusion for consequential, incidental, and punitive damages.

2) SLA/service credits — we need confirmation in writing that service credits under the SLA will be the sole and exclusive remedy for unavailability/performance issues tied to the Platform, and how that interacts with the liability cap (i.e., are credits included in, or separate from, the monetary cap).

3) Carve-outs — we want carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, IP indemnity, and willful misconduct.

Please let us know Redwood's position on whether: (a) credits are included in the liability cap; (b) you will accept the 12-month-fees cap; and (c) whether the sole-remedy language applies only to SLA credits or broader.

If you prefer, we can set a short call to align. Procurement would like to get this finalized before the quarter close.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Celsius Health

Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: liability caps & SLA credit interaction — proposed redline language

Monica / Marissa — drafting notes and proposed text below. High-level approach: preserve a commercially reasonable aggregate cap tied to fees, keep the SLA-credit sole-remedy limited to SLA claims (not IP/confidentiality/bodily injury), and make explicit that credits do not count as an admission of liability and do not reduce indemnity obligations.

Proposed redlines (for insertion into MSA / Order Form):

1) Limitation of Liability (MSA § X):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, except for (i) Seller's indemnification obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement, (ii) either party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, or (iii) damages arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence, the aggregate liability of either party arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be limited to the greater of (a) USD $250,000, or (b) the total amounts paid by Customer to Seller under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."

Notes: we used a dual floor (fixed minimum + 12 months) to protect Redwood on very small pilots while giving Celsius a meaningful cap. We can change the fixed floor if commercial prefers.

2) Exclusion of Consequential Damages (MSA § Y):
"Except as set forth in the preceding sentence, neither party shall be liable for any special, indirect, incidental, consequential, exemplary, or punitive damages, including loss of profits, loss of business, or loss of use, even if such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages."

3) SLA — Service Credits as Exclusive Remedy (Order Form / SLA Annex):
"With respect to availability or performance of the Platform as measured under the SLA, Customer's exclusive and sole remedy shall be the service credit remedies expressly set forth in the SLA Annex to the Order Form. Service credits shall be the exclusive remedy for outages or performance degradations subject to the SLA and shall not be combined with or offset by other monetary damages recoverable under this Agreement, except that such exclusive remedy shall not limit Customer's rights for: (a) breach of confidentiality, (b) indemnity for third-party IP claims, or (c) damages resulting from willful misconduct or gross negligence."

4) Interaction language (to be explicit):
"The payment or application of any service credits under the SLA shall not be deemed to be a waiver of Customer's rights under Section X (Limitation of Liability) with respect to claims other than those covered by the SLA, nor shall the provision of service credits reduce Seller's obligations under Sections relating to indemnity or confidentiality."

Commercial trade-offs: we recommend the 12-month lookback + $250k floor. If sales wants a lower cap or no floor, let us know and we'll prepare alternate wording.

Karthik

Monica / Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline.

High level — legal and procurement reviewed and can accept Redwood's approach in principle with two requests: (1) reduce the floor from $250k to $100k (Celsius handles relatively small pilots and the higher floor is punitive for our budget), and (2) we propose a cap equal to the greater of (a) USD $100,000 or (b) total amounts paid in the prior six (6) months (rather than 12).

Regarding SLA credits as sole remedy — we are fine with credits being the exclusive remedy for SLA incidents, provided there is an explicit sentence confirming that service credits are not considered "monetary damages" that would otherwise reduce the cap (i.e., they should sit outside the cap, or at a minimum not be double-counted). If Redwood prefers credits to count against the cap, we need the lower 6-month window.

We've attached our redline for your review (Doc: redline_from_celsius_20260912.docx) and can hop on a 30-minute call Monday morning to finalize numbers.

Alex Johnson
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Celsius Health
